chunks: And by this chain: from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him),
who said: "Performing istinja' with the right hand is (an act of) rudeness (jafāʾ)."

Then the author (may Allah the Exalted support him) said: "…until the najasah is removed. He did not set a specific limit for it, so what is indicated by it [is that cleansing continues until full removal of the impurity]."

key_terms.الِاسْتِنْجَاءُ: istinja' — ritual cleansing of the private parts after relieving oneself
key_terms.الْجَفَاءِ: jafa' — rudeness, coarseness, a breach of proper Islamic conduct

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq (AS) say about performing istinja' with the right hand, and what is the ruling on how long istinja' must continue?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) declares that performing istinja' (post-toilet cleansing of the private parts) with the right hand constitutes jafa' (rudeness/improper conduct), reflecting the broader Islamic principle of reserving the right hand for honorable acts. The juristic commentary appended by the author (likely Shaykh al-Tusi) clarifies that the cleansing must continue until the najasah is fully removed, and since the Imam prescribed no fixed numerical limit, that removal itself is the operative criterion.
